rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

Covenant ratio values are not printed for 2025-12-31 or 2026-09-30; the last printed values are fixed charge coverage of 2.15x and leverage of 3.07x at 2024-12-31, which are outdated, so covenant headroom is not established. This is a high-severity gap, and the compliance figures with the credit agreement definitions would close it. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21

No maturity schedule is printed at 2026-09-30, so the debt maturities table uses the ladder at 2025-12-31, which omits the USD 150.0 million bridge facility and the USD 39.8 million variable-rate note to finance companies and shows the mortgage and sidecar facilities before their 2026 repayments. This is a high-severity gap, and a current schedule by year would close it. Basis: calculation C19; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 16–21

The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from its own reconciliation lines and every ratio on it depends on that derivation. This is a medium-severity gap, and the issuer's own unadjusted figure would close it. Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94

The legal rank of the secured facilities against one another and against the notes to finance companies is not stated, so no debt stack and no senior secured debt figure are stated and senior secured debt over EBITDA is not calculable for any period. This is a medium-severity gap, and the credit agreement and intercreditor terms would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 50

Floor plan facility availability is not stated, so undrawn committed facilities count only revolving credit and mortgage availability and understate total undrawn capacity. This is a medium-severity gap, and availability by floor plan facility would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 87

The filings print a dash for nine months 2025 other income (expense), net, for the FY2025 gain on acquisition of equity interest and for nine months 2025 proceeds from borrowings, and the quarterly statements do not print the gain on acquisition of equity interest line, so those cells are not supplied rather than zero; the FY2024 net cash change is also left unsupported, and no interest income line is printed. These are low-severity gaps that do not affect any total used in the ratios. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 124–125; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 8; calculation C6

The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed on its own, so only revenue and adjusted EBITDA are derived for it, and no Q3 2024 quarter is supplied, so growth rates for Q3 2025 are not stated. These are low-severity gaps, and the 2025 quarterly reports would close them. Basis: calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 93

The split of capital expenditure between maintenance and growth is not disclosed, so only total capital expenditure is carried and the related ratios are not calculated. This is a low-severity gap. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 89

Finance short-term lease liabilities rose to USD 120.9 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 19.2 million at 2025-12-31, and the sections read give no explanation, so a near-term cash claim cannot be ruled out; the amount sits outside total debt. This is a low-severity gap. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 6

The aggregate of the dividend approved for payment on 2027-01-15 is not stated, so its effect on net debt is not supplied. This is a low-severity gap, and the record-date share count would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 91

Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed, so the debt instruments table carries principal with one aggregate financing cost adjustment; the total commitment of the mortgage and sidecar facilities, the amortisation of the bridge facility and of the notes to finance companies, and the legal rank of the revolving credit facility are also not stated. These are low-severity gaps, and the credit agreements would close them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 16–21

The 2024 annual report states that the parent company has no independent assets or operations and that the one non-guarantor operating subsidiary is minor, but the 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports do not repeat it, and no guarantor-level statements are printed. This is a low-severity gap. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 19

facts.text: One family group controls the vote, and no independent check on how it uses that control is evident. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder payouts are the clearest creditor-adverse pattern: dividends plus repurchases were 113.05% of net income in the first nine months of 2026 and 110.53% in FY2025, against 34.81% in FY2024, and they ran alongside acquisition spending. Two facts soften the point: FY2025 net income carried a USD 173.8 million non-cash impairment, and there were no repurchases in the third quarter of 2026. Against that, the issuer's own measure of earnings free of distribution restrictions fell by USD 109.1 million in the first quarter alone, to USD 282.0 million at 2026-03-31, and it is not printed after that date. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-04-30_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 18, 61; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 90

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Creditor protections were loosened in 2024 and compliance cannot be tracked. The March 2024 amendment extended the credit agreement to 2029-03-13 but raised the unrestricted dividend basket from USD 0.12 to USD 0.18 per share and removed the consolidated liquidity ratio covenant, and the remaining tests of 1.20x minimum fixed charge coverage and 5.75x maximum lease-adjusted leverage have printed values only at 2024-12-31, when they were 2.15x and 3.07x. The guarantees of the EchoPark subsidiaries on the senior notes may be released in certain circumstances, which could move a segment that produced 8.01% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA out of the noteholder guarantee group. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Several facts argue for lower risk than medium. The controlling holders own 38.05% of the shares, so they bear a large part of any loss in value; manufacturer approval rights and the noteholders' right to require repurchase on a change of control protect creditors if control changes; the statements are audited; the related-party total is only 2.38% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA; and USD 282.0 million of earnings was still free of distribution restrictions at 2026-03-31. A proxy statement showing an independent board majority and independent review of affiliate dealings, together with payouts back below earnings, would support a low risk level. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Other facts argue for higher risk. Payouts above net income, a 2024 amendment that widened the dividend basket and removed the liquidity covenant, covenant values that are no longer printed and a controlling group that sets policy without an evident independent check could together justify a high rating if the remaining restricted-payments capacity proves small. The view would move to high if capacity at 2026-09-30 is shown to be nearly used, if a debt-funded distribution, an exchange offer or a release of the EchoPark guarantees is announced, or if affiliate payments rise well above USD 14.6 million; later compliance figures and the full credit agreements would show how close the tests are. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 91

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Sonic has spent heavily on acquisitions across 2025 and 2026 and paid for them with floor plan inventory financing, cash and new term debt, so creditors are underwriting a growing business whose acquisitions are only beginning to show in earnings. The 2025 purchase of five Jaguar Land Rover dealerships cost USD 440.3 million, of which USD 166.1 million was inventory funded by floor plan notes, and the nine months of 2026 added a Powersports business of six locations and a Porsche store for USD 169.3 million, which contributed USD 51.8 million of revenue and USD 2.2 million of pre-tax income. The company prints pro forma revenue and pre-tax income for these deals but no pro forma EBITDA, and the Powersports business could not be included in the 2026 pro forma figures. Basis: calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 138; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

facts.label: Industry forces
facts.text: Rivalry is high: the industry is fragmented, competitors include larger multi-franchise groups, and internet sellers and brokers narrow price differences on new vehicles, which pressures margin per unit. New entrants are limited by state franchise laws, but direct-to-consumer sellers have succeeded in some states and manufacturers have introduced agency sales in European markets, a risk to new vehicle profit pools if extended. Buyers hold power over new vehicle price through internet price comparison; suppliers, meaning the manufacturers, hold power through production levels, incentives, facility image requirements and approval rights over ownership. The substitution risk is the move of sales from dealers to manufacturers, not another product. facts.text: Overall, Sonic presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring service and finance income, a franchise base spread across 24 brands and long-dated senior notes, but credit quality is constrained by falling franchised earnings, payouts funded by borrowing and a concentrated 2027 refinancing. Cash-flow durability appears adequate on the fixed operations base and weak once payouts and acquisitions are included. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on lender appetite for USD 561.2 million of bridge and mortgage debt, the level of covenant headroom and the price of the senior notes, which sit at 91.50% and 94.51% of par. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings are enough to run Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit on Sonic Automotive Inc's own disclosures, but covenant headroom and ratings-based triggers cannot be tested independently, so creditors should treat those two points as open.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 112–114

The latest filing covers the quarter ended 2026-09-30 and was signed on 2026-10-29. The covenant tests are printed, at a minimum fixed charge coverage of 1.20x and a maximum lease-adjusted leverage of 5.75x, but the issuer's own ratio values are printed only at 2024-12-31, and no agency rating is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 98; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107
### Key findings

All five filings are the consolidated reports of Sonic Automotive, Inc., the Delaware parent whose Class A shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange, so debt, earnings and liquidity are read at one perimeter and no parent-versus-subsidiary conflict arises in the sources. The senior notes are guaranteed by the domestic operating subsidiaries, and none of the filings prints separate financial statements for the guarantor group; only the 2024 annual report states that the parent company has no independent assets or operations.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 147; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 19

The supplied periods cover two fiscal years and three consecutive quarters of 2026, which is enough to build a latest-twelve-months view from the fourth quarter of 2025 plus the first nine months of 2026. The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed on its own and has to be derived from the annual figures less the nine-month comparative, and the 2026 quarterly revenue amounts agree to the printed nine-month total.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 5

The debt note ties to the balance sheet at 2026-09-30 and the liquidity table adds up to USD 585.2 million, so the issuer's printed debt and liquidity figures are internally consistent. The long-term debt table excludes floor plan notes payable of USD 2,288.0 million and the lease liabilities, so the debt perimeter has to be set explicitly in the analyses and not read from a single balance sheet line.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 16–17, 87

Covenant testing is the main limit. The filings print the two maintenance tests and state that the issuer remained in compliance, but only the annual report for 2024 prints ratio values, and the credit agreements that define the ratios are listed as exhibits without being supplied. No agency rating appears in any filing.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 112–114, 149; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21

For Business & governance the annual report prints the business description, the executive officers, the voting control held through Class B shares by entities that the chairman and his family control, and the related-party transactions, but directors, board independence, compensation and beneficial ownership are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied.
The latest filing was signed 20 days before the as-of date, and nothing dated after the cutoff is used as fact.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 98
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against proceeding is that every source is the issuer's own filing, so nothing independently confirms covenant compliance, ratings or market pricing, and the debt perimeter choice, with floor plan notes and leases outside the long-term debt table, can change any leverage figure. The view would weaken to not ready for Fundamental credit if the credit agreements define the covenant ratios differently from the filings' summaries, and it would strengthen with the credit agreements, the two indentures, agency ratings and the 2026 proxy statement.
Basis: calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 21
### Limitations

Each filing is available only as extracted text, in chunks that the page references here follow, so original formatting and table layout are not available and the original HTML files are not among the supplied sources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 1

This module records readiness only and makes no credit judgement; its calculations are tie-outs of printed figures. Run settings leave ratings, quotes, peers, deal terms, portfolio limits and legal documents empty, and those blanks are treated as not supplied, not as zero.

## Gaps

The credit agreements, the two senior note indentures, the mortgage and sidecar facility agreements, the bridge facility agreement and the subsidiary guaranty agreements are listed as exhibits in the filings but are not supplied. Without them the definitions behind the fixed charge coverage and lease-adjusted leverage tests, the security package and the guarantor group cannot be read from the primary documents, and the analyses must rely on the issuer's own note summaries. This is a material gap for Fundamental credit; supplying the agreements would let Legal & covenants and Recovery & fulcrum run on governing text.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 112–114; 10-Q_2026-04-30_sah.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21

The issuer's own covenant ratio values are printed only at 2024-12-31, where fixed charge coverage was 2.15x against a minimum of 1.20x and lease-adjusted leverage was 3.07x against a maximum of 5.75x. The annual report for 2025 and the three 2026 quarterly reports print the levels and state continuing compliance but no ratio value, so headroom at 2025-12-31 and at 2026-09-30 is not established, and the 2024 values are outdated for the as-of date and must not be carried forward as current. This is a material gap.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 107, 164; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21

No agency rating appears in any filing, and the run settings supply no ratings, bond or loan quotes, peer set, deal terms or portfolio limits. Ratings-based triggers, market-implied spreads, peer benchmarking and portfolio fit are therefore not established, and the issuer-disclosed fair values of the two senior note series are the only debt pricing figures in the filings. The annual report's one mention of a corporate credit rating is as an input to a lease discount rate and gives no rating. This is a minor gap for the three requested analyses.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 171; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25

Directors, board independence and committees, executive and director compensation, beneficial ownership and the policies on affiliate transactions are incorporated by reference to the 2026 proxy statement, which is not supplied. The annual report's own passages on control, executive officers and related parties cover part of this, so governance can be assessed but not completely. This is a minor gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 110

The 2026 quarterly reports print no maturity schedule by year, so the debt maturity profile at 2026-09-30 has to be assembled from the individual facility descriptions. The last printed schedule is at 2025-12-31, does not include the bridge facility, and is outdated for later dates. This is a minor gap.
Basis: calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 16–21

The 2024 annual report states that the parent company has no independent assets or operations and that the one non-domestic operating subsidiary that is not a guarantor is minor. The 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports state the guarantee by the domestic operating subsidiaries but not those two statements, so the guarantor perimeter at 2026-09-30 rests on a 2024 statement that is outdated, and no guarantor-level financial statements are printed. This is a minor gap.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 19

No 2025 quarterly reports, earnings releases, investor presentations or management projections were supplied. The fourth quarter of 2025 is therefore derived, and the 2025 comparatives are as shown in the 2026 filings, so originally reported 2025 quarters cannot be tied to them. This is a minor gap.
Basis: calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 5

The file names do not follow one date convention: the two annual reports and the second-quarter report carry the period end, while the first- and third-quarter reports carry the signature date. Periods in this run are taken from each filing's cover page and not from its file name. This is a minor gap.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Debt of 3.06x LTM reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 looks better than 3.62x at 2025-12-31 only because the 2025 impairment dropped out; adjusted leverage rose from 2.63x to 2.97x, so creditors face weaker earnings on higher debt, not deleveraging.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 93–94; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 104, 122

Reported operating cash flow was negative over the first nine months of 2026 as inventories rose, floor plan funding paid for the build, and issuer-defined liquidity fell to USD 585.2 million from USD 701.6 million at year-end. Covenant ratios are not printed after 2024-12-31, so headroom cannot be confirmed.
Basis: calculation C25; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 21, 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107
### Key findings

Total debt at carrying value rose to USD 1,749.7 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 1,615.4 million at 2025-12-31, and net debt is USD 1,739.0 million, or USD 1,752.0 million pro forma for a dividend paid after the quarter on 2026-10-15. Principal rose by USD 130.2 million, from a USD 150.0 million bridge facility and a USD 39.8 million variable-rate note to finance companies, partly offset by USD 44.6 million of reductions in the mortgage and sidecar facilities and USD 15.0 million of reductions in the fixed-rate notes. Reported net leverage is 3.04x, or 3.06x pro forma, against 3.60x at year-end, but the fall reflects the USD 173.8 million FY2025 impairment leaving the LTM base; on adjusted EBITDA net leverage rose from 2.62x to 2.95x.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C19; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 104, 145

LTM adjusted EBITDA of USD 589.5 million is USD 25.1 million below the USD 614.6 million of FY2025, and the decline sits in the Franchised Dealerships Segment, whose LTM adjusted EBITDA is USD 524.9 million against USD 553.9 million in FY2025, while EchoPark held at USD 49.2 million and Powersports rose to USD 15.4 million from USD 11.5 million. In Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA was USD 134.4 million against USD 149.4 million a year earlier, down USD 15.0 million or 10.04%, while revenue was nearly flat at USD 3,988.8 million against USD 3,973.8 million; selling, general and administrative expenses rose USD 15.2 million to USD 466.8 million while gross profit rose only USD 2.0 million to USD 617.5 million, so the pressure is cost growth, not volume.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C22; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 93–94; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 104

EBITDA covers cash interest 2.87x on the reported LTM basis and 2.96x on the adjusted basis, against 2.36x and 3.24x in FY2025; the reported cover rose because the impairment left the base, while the adjusted cover fell because adjusted EBITDA slipped and cash interest rose. Cover is conservative because cash interest paid of USD 198.9 million includes floor plan interest, which the EBITDA used here already deducts; adding LTM floor plan interest of USD 87.2 million back to reported EBITDA gives 3.31x.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 125

Reported operating cash flow for the nine months of 2026 was USD -14.5 million as inventories absorbed USD 415.4 million; floor plan notes funded the build mainly in financing cash flow, and on the issuer's alternative basis operating cash flow was USD 424.2 million against USD 729.7 million for the nine months of 2025. The floor plan funding appears as USD 438.7 million of non-trade financing and USD 26.6 million of trade operating flow, USD 465.3 million in all, and the combined figure is the one that serves the alternative basis. LTM operating cash flow is USD 52.4 million as printed and USD 276.3 million on that basis, against LTM capital expenditure of USD 261.0 million, so LTM free cash flow is USD -208.6 million as printed and USD 15.3 million on the alternative basis, before USD 169.3 million of acquisitions and USD 142.0 million of share repurchases in the nine months.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C24; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 91–92

Issuer-defined liquidity resources fell by USD 116.4 million to USD 585.2 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 701.6 million at 2025-12-31, of which USD 110.0 million is the floor plan deposit balance falling to USD 190.0 million from USD 300.0 million. Cash plus committed undrawn availability is USD 395.2 million, against USD 401.6 million at year-end and USD 521.6 million at 2024-12-31, which is 0.23x total debt against 0.25x and 0.33x; the balance-sheet cash balance is only USD 10.7 million, and pro forma cash after the dividend paid on 2026-10-15 is not established.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C25; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 99

The latest maturity ladder the filings print is at 2025-12-31, with USD 1,635.2 million of principal, USD 416.2 million due in 2027 and USD 651.0 million in 2029. At 2026-09-30 the USD 150.0 million bridge facility, due within 364 days of its closing or earlier on a refinancing of the mortgage facility, and the USD 411.2 million mortgage and sidecar facilities, which amortise through 2027 and mature in 2027, together are USD 561.2 million to repay or refinance by the end of 2027, and USD 193.3 million is already classed as current.
Basis: calculation C19; calculation C5; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 16–17, 20–21

Total debt excludes floor plan notes payable of USD 2,288.0 million, which the issuer treats as inventory financing, and finance and operating lease liabilities of USD 407.1 million and USD 278.8 million; including floor plan notes would put LTM total debt at 7.06x reported EBITDA and including finance leases at 3.77x, so every leverage figure here states its perimeter. Reported EBITDA is not printed by the issuer and is derived from its own reconciliation lines, with floor plan interest and impairment left as expenses.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C15; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 89, 93–94

The financial covenants are a minimum fixed charge coverage of 1.20x and a maximum lease-adjusted leverage of 5.75x, and the issuer states compliance at 2026-09-30, but the last printed ratio values are 2.15x and 3.07x at 2024-12-31; no ratio value is printed for 2025-12-31 or 2026-09-30, and this module does not infer covenant headroom.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107

Two dividends after the quarter-end are kept out of period figures: USD 13.0 million paid on 2026-10-15, which lifts pro forma net debt to USD 1,752.0 million, and a further USD 0.41 per share payable on 2027-01-15 whose aggregate is not stated.
Basis: calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 91

Statement identities hold at every date except the FY2024 cash flow, where the three printed activity totals sum to USD 15.2 million but the filing prints a net change of USD 15.1 million, so that net change is left unsupported. Where the filing prints a dash the cell is not supplied, not zero; the exception is the issuer's own EBITDA reconciliation, where dashes mean no adjustment because the printed totals reconcile only on that reading.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 125
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that credit is firmer than it looks is that reported net leverage of 3.04x, or 3.06x pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-15, is below the 3.60x of year-end, reported cover rose to 2.87x, nine-month net income recovered to USD 159.4 million from USD 71.8 million, and floor plan notes rose USD 355.3 million alongside a USD 430.1 million rise in inventory, so most of the funding growth is matched to stock; the issuer also states compliance with every restrictive covenant. The view would improve if adjusted EBITDA steadies above USD 614.6 million or debt falls, and it would weaken if the franchised segment decline continues into Q4 2026 or the USD 561.2 million of 2027 repayments is refinanced on worse terms.
Basis: calculation C19; calculation C22; calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 21, 93–94
### Limitations

Interim ratios use last-twelve-month figures whose 2025 comparative columns are as shown in the 2026 quarterly reports, because no 2025 quarterly reports are supplied; the legal rank of the facilities, the covenant definitions, ratings and a current maturity schedule are not in the sources, and the source readiness assessment lists the agreements that are not supplied.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 5
This module states figures and tie-outs only; it makes no covenant, ranking or recovery judgement, and every ratio is on carrying-value debt with the perimeter stated.

## Gaps

Covenant ratio values are not printed for 2025-12-31 or 2026-09-30; the last printed values are fixed charge coverage of 2.15x and leverage of 3.07x at 2024-12-31, which are outdated, so covenant headroom is not established. This is a high-severity gap, and the compliance figures with the credit agreement definitions would close it.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21

No maturity schedule is printed at 2026-09-30, so the debt maturities table uses the ladder at 2025-12-31, which omits the USD 150.0 million bridge facility and the USD 39.8 million variable-rate note to finance companies and shows the mortgage and sidecar facilities before their 2026 repayments. This is a high-severity gap, and a current schedule by year would close it.
Basis: calculation C19; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 16–21

The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from its own reconciliation lines and every ratio on it depends on that derivation. This is a medium-severity gap, and the issuer's own unadjusted figure would close it.
Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94

The legal rank of the secured facilities against one another and against the notes to finance companies is not stated, so no debt stack and no senior secured debt figure are stated and senior secured debt over EBITDA is not calculable for any period. This is a medium-severity gap, and the credit agreement and intercreditor terms would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 50

Floor plan facility availability is not stated, so undrawn committed facilities count only revolving credit and mortgage availability and understate total undrawn capacity. This is a medium-severity gap, and availability by floor plan facility would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 87

The filings print a dash for nine months 2025 other income (expense), net, for the FY2025 gain on acquisition of equity interest and for nine months 2025 proceeds from borrowings, and the quarterly statements do not print the gain on acquisition of equity interest line, so those cells are not supplied rather than zero; the FY2024 net cash change is also left unsupported, and no interest income line is printed. These are low-severity gaps that do not affect any total used in the ratios.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 124–125; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 8; calculation C6

The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed on its own, so only revenue and adjusted EBITDA are derived for it, and no Q3 2024 quarter is supplied, so growth rates for Q3 2025 are not stated. These are low-severity gaps, and the 2025 quarterly reports would close them.
Basis: calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 93
The split of capital expenditure between maintenance and growth is not disclosed, so only total capital expenditure is carried and the related ratios are not calculated. This is a low-severity gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 89

Finance short-term lease liabilities rose to USD 120.9 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 19.2 million at 2025-12-31, and the sections read give no explanation, so a near-term cash claim cannot be ruled out; the amount sits outside total debt. This is a low-severity gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 6
The aggregate of the dividend approved for payment on 2027-01-15 is not stated, so its effect on net debt is not supplied. This is a low-severity gap, and the record-date share count would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 91

Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed, so the debt instruments table carries principal with one aggregate financing cost adjustment; the total commitment of the mortgage and sidecar facilities, the amortisation of the bridge facility and of the notes to finance companies, and the legal rank of the revolving credit facility are also not stated. These are low-severity gaps, and the credit agreements would close them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 16–21

The 2024 annual report states that the parent company has no independent assets or operations and that the one non-guarantor operating subsidiary is minor, but the 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports do not repeat it, and no guarantor-level statements are printed. This is a low-severity gap.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 19

## Findings
### Bottom line

Control by one family and heavy shareholder payouts leave creditors reliant on covenants rather than on governance, while acquisitions and weaker new vehicle margins add pressure; governance risk is medium, not high.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38, 154; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 90

Class B shares carry 86.00% of the votes on 38.05% of the shares, and dividends plus repurchases took 113.05% of nine-month 2026 net income while USD 609.6 million went on acquisitions across 2025 and 2026. Audited reporting, small affiliate payments of 2.38% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA and no described waiver or exchange keep the risk below high.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 138, 152–153; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 12–13
### Key findings

One family group controls the vote, and no independent check on how it uses that control is evident. Class B shares carry 86.00% of the votes on 38.05% of shares outstanding, and six of the nine people who signed the 2025 annual report as Chairman or director hold executive roles at Sonic or officer or director roles at companies the controlling family owns; whether any director is independent is not stated in the filings read. Manufacturers hold approval rights over ownership and board changes, so control is hard to transfer, but creditors have no governance voice of their own.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 37–38, 118, 152–153; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 2

Shareholder payouts are the clearest creditor-adverse pattern: dividends plus repurchases were 113.05% of net income in the first nine months of 2026 and 110.53% in FY2025, against 34.81% in FY2024, and they ran alongside acquisition spending. Two facts soften the point: FY2025 net income carried a USD 173.8 million non-cash impairment, and there were no repurchases in the third quarter of 2026. Against that, the issuer's own measure of earnings free of distribution restrictions fell by USD 109.1 million in the first quarter alone, to USD 282.0 million at 2026-03-31, and it is not printed after that date.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-04-30_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 18, 61; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 90

Acquisitions have been funded ahead of earnings. USD 609.6 million was spent across 2025 and nine months 2026, including USD 440.3 million for five Jaguar Land Rover dealerships, while the 2026 acquisitions contributed only USD 2.2 million of pre-tax income so far and pro forma EBITDA is not printed. The history shows growth plans can reverse at cost: the 2023 suspension of EchoPark locations carried a charge of about USD 75.2 million, and the 2025 franchise asset test required a USD 172.4 million impairment, so spending and payouts sit alongside real write-downs.
Basis: calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 138, 141; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 16, 84

Related-party leakage is small today but unchecked. Affiliates of the controlling holders received USD 14.6 million of 2025 expense, which is 2.38% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, mostly naming rights for the Atlanta speedway and aircraft arrangements, and the company states that the majority of affiliate arrangements have not been verified by third parties; 2026 amounts are not printed because the quarterly reports contain no related-party note.
Basis: calculation C5; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 152–153

Creditor protections were loosened in 2024 and compliance cannot be tracked. The March 2024 amendment extended the credit agreement to 2029-03-13 but raised the unrestricted dividend basket from USD 0.12 to USD 0.18 per share and removed the consolidated liquidity ratio covenant, and the remaining tests of 1.20x minimum fixed charge coverage and 5.75x maximum lease-adjusted leverage have printed values only at 2024-12-31, when they were 2.15x and 3.07x. The guarantees of the EchoPark subsidiaries on the senior notes may be released in certain circumstances, which could move a segment that produced 8.01% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA out of the noteholder guarantee group.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C15; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103, 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147, 149; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 21

The business behind the credit is steadier than its vehicle sales suggest, which is the main reason the risk is medium. Fixed operations plus finance and insurance produced 78.00% of gross profit in the first nine months of 2026 from 18.98% of revenue, and the Franchised Dealerships Segment produced 90.12% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA; against that, same-store new vehicle unit sales fell 6%, gross profit per new vehicle fell USD 226 to USD 2,957 and days supply rose to 65 days from 51 days, so the profit pool that funds payouts is under pressure.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

Disclosure and audit are supportive. Grant Thornton audited FY2024 and FY2025 and the controls over financial reporting, management concluded that disclosure controls were effective at 2026-09-30, and no waiver, exchange offer, priming transaction or equity cure is described in the filings read; that is an absence of disclosure, not proof that no such event occurred.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 129, 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 119–121; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 97
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

Several facts argue for lower risk than medium. The controlling holders own 38.05% of the shares, so they bear a large part of any loss in value; manufacturer approval rights and the noteholders' right to require repurchase on a change of control protect creditors if control changes; the statements are audited; the related-party total is only 2.38% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA; and USD 282.0 million of earnings was still free of distribution restrictions at 2026-03-31. A proxy statement showing an independent board majority and independent review of affiliate dealings, together with payouts back below earnings, would support a low risk level.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 35, 37–38; 10-Q_2026-04-30_sah.htm.jsonl, page 18

Other facts argue for higher risk. Payouts above net income, a 2024 amendment that widened the dividend basket and removed the liquidity covenant, covenant values that are no longer printed and a controlling group that sets policy without an evident independent check could together justify a high rating if the remaining restricted-payments capacity proves small. The view would move to high if capacity at 2026-09-30 is shown to be nearly used, if a debt-funded distribution, an exchange offer or a release of the EchoPark guarantees is announced, or if affiliate payments rise well above USD 14.6 million; later compliance figures and the full credit agreements would show how close the tests are.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 91
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee membership, the affiliate review policy and holdings by named holder are not established; the control conclusion stands, but the medium risk level could move one step either way once the board and policy are known.

- The issuer's own measure of earnings free of distribution restrictions is printed only at 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31, and its definition sits in agreements outside the filings, so the payout conclusion cannot be tested against the limit at 2026-09-30; if the remaining capacity proved small, the risk level would rise.

- Acquisition funding beyond inventory financing is not itemised and no pro forma EBITDA is printed, so the acquisition conclusion rests on spending and early earnings contribution rather than on returns.
- Related-party amounts are available for 2025 only, so the finding of low leakage applies to 2025 and affiliate payments in 2026 could differ.

- Support from the controlling holders and any waiver or amendment history are judged from the absence of disclosure in five filings, so the finding that no creditor-adverse liability management has occurred is a limit of the documents read, not proof.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Sonic has spent heavily on acquisitions across 2025 and 2026 and paid for them with floor plan inventory financing, cash and new term debt, so creditors are underwriting a growing business whose acquisitions are only beginning to show in earnings. The 2025 purchase of five Jaguar Land Rover dealerships cost USD 440.3 million, of which USD 166.1 million was inventory funded by floor plan notes, and the nine months of 2026 added a Powersports business of six locations and a Porsche store for USD 169.3 million, which contributed USD 51.8 million of revenue and USD 2.2 million of pre-tax income. The company prints pro forma revenue and pre-tax income for these deals but no pro forma EBITDA, and the Powersports business could not be included in the 2026 pro forma figures.
Basis: calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 138; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

New debt in the period is a USD 149.1 million sidecar term loan drawn on 2025-10-24 and a USD 150.0 million bridge facility borrowed on 2026-03-27, an unsecured term loan that matures on the earlier of 364 days after closing and a refinancing of the mortgage facility; proceeds from borrowings of USD 190.0 million in the nine-month 2026 cash flow statement include the bridge facility. The senior notes of USD 650.0 million due 2029 and USD 500.0 million due 2031 date from the 2021 financing of the RFJ Auto Partners acquisition and are unchanged, and the March 2024 amendment of the credit agreement extended its maturity to 2029-03-13 with commitments of USD 2.4 billion.

Disposals and shareholder returns run the other way: five locations were sold for USD 62.7 million, while repurchases of USD 142.0 million and dividends of USD 38.2 million were paid in the nine months, with no repurchases in the third quarter. The Board added USD 500.0 million to the repurchase authorization on 2026-04-30, leaving USD 527.9 million at 2026-09-30. No sponsor or equity contribution is described, and the split between cash, floor plan and borrowings for acquisitions beyond inventory financing is not itemised.

## Findings
### Bottom line
Sonic is an adequate but weakening credit: earnings are slipping on new vehicle margins and overhead while debt, shareholder payouts and 2027 repayments rise, and covenant headroom cannot be seen.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7

Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 589.5 million over the last twelve months from USD 614.6 million in FY2025 while total debt rose to USD 1,749.7 million, lifting adjusted leverage to 2.97x from 2.63x. Fixed operations and finance and insurance supply 78.00% of gross profit and cushion the decline, but USD 561.2 million of debt falls due by the end of 2027 against USD 395.2 million of cash and undrawn facilities.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C13
### Key findings

Earnings are falling where it matters most, and the cause is overhead as much as volume. The Franchised Dealerships Segment earned USD 189.7 million before tax and impairment in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 244.4 million, a fall of 22.38%, and total segment income fell 18.29% to USD 223.3 million. In that segment gross profit rose USD 22.7 million while selling, general and administrative expenses rose USD 76.8 million, and across the group those expenses took 73.04% of gross profit against 69.75%.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 73–76

Leverage on adjusted earnings has risen even though reported leverage looks better. Total debt of USD 1,749.7 million is 2.97x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA against 2.63x at 2025-12-31, while on reported EBITDA it is 3.06x against 3.62x, a fall that comes only from the 2025 impairment leaving the base. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 2.96x against 3.24x. These ratios use carrying-value debt and leave out floor plan notes of USD 2,288.0 million and leases.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C14

Cash flow does not cover growth and payouts. On the issuer's alternative basis, in which all floor plan changes are operating, operating cash flow of USD 424.2 million less investing outflows of USD 329.7 million left USD 94.5 million, against USD 180.2 million of dividends and repurchases, so the USD 85.7 million gap was met by net new borrowing of USD 90.1 million. As printed, operating cash flow was USD -14.5 million because inventories rose.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 92

Liquidity is thinner and 2027 is the refinancing year. Issuer-defined liquidity fell USD 116.4 million to USD 585.2 million, USD 110.0 million of it from the floor plan deposit, and cash plus committed undrawn facilities of USD 395.2 million cover the USD 561.2 million of bridge and mortgage debt due by the end of 2027 only 0.70x. The USD 1,150.0 million of senior notes do not mature until 2029 and 2031, but the issuer's market quotations value the 2031 notes at 91.50% of par and the 2029 notes at 94.51%, down from 95.76% and 97.00% at 2025-12-31, a move the filings do not split between rates and credit.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C11; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 24, 87

Interest cost depends on short-term rates with little protection. Variable-rate debt is USD 2.7 billion, a 1.0% rise in rates would add USD 20.4 million of interest over nine months, equal to 4.63% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, and the interest rate caps on USD 1,000.0 million of notional pay only above 5.50% against one-month SOFR of 3.91%, with USD 400.0 million of them expiring on 2026-12-31. Floor plan rates have fallen, from a weighted average of 5.66% to 4.99% over nine months, which helps, although floor plan interest expense still rose USD 2.5 million to USD 64.7 million on larger balances.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 88, 96

Inventory is building into a softer new vehicle market. New vehicle inventories rose USD 269.3 million, or 23.62%, days supply is 65 days against 51 days a year earlier, same-store retail new vehicle unit sales fell 6% and gross profit per new vehicle fell USD 226 to USD 2,957. Management estimates 2026 new vehicle industry volume at 1% to 3% below the 2025 level, so volume is not expected to recover this year.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 32–33

Two stabilisers keep the credit adequate. Fixed operations and finance and insurance produced 78.00% of gross profit in nine months 2026 from 18.98% of revenue, with a fixed operations gross margin of 51.2%; and management has levers, because 73.71% of capital expenditure was construction and real estate projects, no shares were repurchased in the third quarter and land and buildings at cost of USD 2,144.3 million can be mortgaged or sold.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C13; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 34, 87, 89–90

Financial policy is the weakest part of the profile. One family controls 86.00% of the votes, dividends plus repurchases were 113.05% of nine-month 2026 net income, and the issuer's measure of earnings free of distribution restrictions fell USD 109.1 million to USD 282.0 million in the first quarter and has not been printed since; covenant ratio values were last printed for 2024-12-31. Business & governance rates the sponsor and governance risk as medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-04-30_sah.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that credit is firmer than it looks is that reported leverage fell to 3.06x from 3.62x, adjusted leverage of 2.97x remains under three times EBITDA, recurring service and finance income supplies most gross profit, and management can stop repurchases, defer construction and raise cash against owned real estate. Sonic has a record of extending and adding bank facilities, with the credit agreement extended to 2029-03-13 in March 2024 and the sidecar facility added in December 2024, and the senior notes do not fall due until 2029. The view would improve if adjusted EBITDA steadies above USD 614.6 million, if overhead falls back toward 69.75% of gross profit, or if the 2027 facilities are extended early.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C9; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 146, 148

The strongest case that credit is weaker than it looks is that the payout and acquisition programme is already financed by borrowing while adjusted EBITDA falls, that inventory and floor plan balances are rising into a market where industry volume is expected to fall, and that covenant values are not printed so creditors cannot confirm headroom. The view would weaken if the fourth quarter repeats the 10.04% fall in adjusted EBITDA seen in the third quarter, if days supply stays above 65 days into 2027, if the bridge facility is refinanced at higher cost, or if repurchases resume under the USD 527.9 million authorization.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 90
### Limitations

- No rating, lender statement or price history is supplied beyond the issuer's quarter-end note quotations, so the 2027 refinancing conclusion judges market access from the issuer's own disclosures; wider spreads than those quotations imply would worsen it.

- The downside path is qualitative: no management projection, no covenant ratio value after 2024-12-31 and no segment-level debt is printed, so the scenario names causes and observable triggers but not the point at which a covenant would be breached or liquidity would run out.
- No peer figures are supplied, so adequate is judged against Sonic's own history and the industry data the issuer quotes; against other dealer groups the profile could rank higher or lower.

- Interim comparisons mix acquired and existing stores and same-store data are printed only for some lines, so how much of the 2026 earnings change is organic is partly unknown; the pressure on franchised earnings could be overstated if acquired stores are still ramping.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strengths, in order of weight, are recurring fixed operations and finance and insurance income, which supply 78.00% of gross profit and so cushion a vehicle downturn; long-dated senior notes of USD 1,150.0 million that mature in 2029 and 2031; discretionary capital spending, with 73.71% of the total in construction and real estate projects, and no repurchases in the third quarter; and an owned real estate base of USD 2,144.3 million at cost.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 14, 34, 89–90

The weaknesses, in order of weight, are falling franchised earnings as overhead outgrows gross profit; payouts and acquisitions funded by net new borrowing of USD 90.1 million; USD 561.2 million of bridge and mortgage debt due by the end of 2027 against USD 395.2 million of cash and undrawn facilities; USD 2.7 billion of variable-rate debt with caps that pay only above 5.50%; and covenant ratio values that were last printed for 2024-12-31 under the control of one family that holds 86.00% of the votes.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 22, 26, 73–74, 96; 10-K_2024-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 107
### Company description

Sonic is one of the largest US automotive retailers and earns from three sources: new, used and wholesale vehicle sales, parts, service and collision repair, and finance and insurance commissions. The Franchised Dealerships Segment produced 85.0% of FY2025 revenue across 24 brands, with luxury brands at 63% of franchised new vehicle revenue; EchoPark, a pre-owned retailer, produced 13.7% and Powersports 1.3%. Texas and California together are 50.8% of revenue, so regional demand and regulation matter more than the national spread of stores suggests.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

The model supports debt service unevenly. Service, parts and finance income recur through the cycle, but vehicle sales are discretionary and cyclical, so cash-flow visibility is moderate and depends on how fast inventory turns. Franchise agreements give manufacturers approval rights over ownership changes, which protects the franchise base and limits any change of control; refinancing confidence rests on the franchise value and owned real estate rather than on contracted revenue.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11
### Ownership and group structure

Sonic is publicly listed but controlled: Class B holders led by Sonic Financial Corporation and the OBS Family, LLC carry 86.00% of the votes on 38.05% of the shares, and the Smith family also controls affiliates that do business with the company, with payments of USD 14.6 million in FY2025, or 2.38% of adjusted EBITDA. The operating subsidiaries are wholly owned, apart from one jointly owned dealership, and the domestic operating subsidiaries guarantee the senior notes; the guarantees of the EchoPark subsidiaries may be released in certain circumstances, and the legal rank of the secured facilities against one another is not stated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38, 128, 147, 152–153

For creditors the control structure means payout, leverage and acquisition policy follow the controlling holders, who also carry a 38.05% economic interest; protection comes from the covenants, not from governance, and the proxy statement that would show board independence is not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is mostly discretionary vehicle sales, driven by unit volume, price and mix, and it is cyclical rather than contracted. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 2.92% to USD 11,611.3 million, but the growth came from EchoPark, up 10.59%, and Powersports, up 37.00%, while Franchised Dealerships revenue rose only 1.04% and its retail units fell 0.92%. Pricing power on new vehicles is weak: gross profit per new vehicle fell USD 226 to USD 2,957 as available inventory raised price competition, whereas finance and insurance gross profit per retail unit rose to USD 2,615.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 32–34, 74

Fixed operations are the most predictable line: service capacity added through technician hiring, higher parts and labor prices passed to customers and a gross margin of 51.2% support revenue that does not depend on new vehicle volume. Revenue is therefore recurring in part, cyclical in part and concentrated by region and by brand.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 34
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Overhead is the swing factor. Compensation is 62.75% of selling, general and administrative expenses and is partly commission-based, which flexes with gross profit, but advertising and other expenses follow business activity and the number of stores and other expenses include fixed items that may not change in proportion to gross profit: other expenses rose USD 48.3 million, or 14.65%, in nine months while gross profit rose 2.70%, and overhead reached 75.60% of gross profit in the third quarter against 73.37%. Operating leverage is therefore adverse when gross profit stalls, and the adjusted EBITDA margin has slipped to 3.81% from 4.06%.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 75–76

Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through the commission element and the fixed operations base, but not against a larger fall in new vehicle gross profit combined with higher other expenses, and the first quarter, when overhead is highest against gross profit, is the weakest point in the year. The filings describe cost pass-through only in fixed operations, where higher parts and labor costs were passed on to customers.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76, 95
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending was USD 223.7 million in nine months 2026, up 98.67% from USD 112.6 million, with USD 164.9 million on construction and real estate projects, and all of it was funded from existing cash; commitments of USD 81.3 million are nearly all due within twelve months. Cash interest paid was USD 198.9 million over the last twelve months and includes floor plan interest, and leases add finance lease liabilities of USD 407.1 million and operating lease liabilities of USD 278.8 million outside debt.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 89–90

Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow was weak in 2026: last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD -208.6 million as printed and USD 15.3 million on the alternative basis that treats all floor plan changes as operating, and after acquisitions of USD 169.3 million and payouts of USD 180.2 million the business borrowed. Capital spending is flexible because most of it is discretionary, but the construction commitments reduce that flexibility over the next year.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C14
### Industry forces

Rivalry is high: the industry is fragmented, competitors include larger multi-franchise groups, and internet sellers and brokers narrow price differences on new vehicles, which pressures margin per unit. New entrants are limited by state franchise laws, but direct-to-consumer sellers have succeeded in some states and manufacturers have introduced agency sales in European markets, a risk to new vehicle profit pools if extended. Buyers hold power over new vehicle price through internet price comparison; suppliers, meaning the manufacturers, hold power through production levels, incentives, facility image requirements and approval rights over ownership. The substitution risk is the move of sales from dealers to manufacturers, not another product.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12, 17–18, 28; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 89
### Macro and regulatory factors

Four outside factors matter for credit. Tariffs and trade policy, interest rates, consumer confidence and manufacturer production and incentive levels are among the factors the issuer cites for an industry volume it now puts 1% to 3% below 2025; interest rates also set floor plan and mortgage cost; the expiry of a federal electric vehicle tax credit in the third quarter of 2025 pulled demand forward into that year; and a 2024 systems outage at a third-party provider cut pre-tax income by about USD 47.2 million. State franchise laws and manufacturer policies shape ownership and sales model risk.
Basis: calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 55–56; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are recurring service and finance income, long-dated senior notes and an owned property base; weaknesses are falling franchised earnings, payouts funded by borrowing and unobservable covenant headroom. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the growth of EchoPark and Powersports earnings, where segment income rose, and a normalisation of new vehicle margin per unit as inventories adjust. Threats are further margin compression on a high days supply, higher short-term rates against caps that pay only above 5.50%, direct-sales models that bypass dealers, and a refinancing of USD 561.2 million in 2027 at worse terms.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74, 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, page 18
### Financial profile

The supports are a recurring profit base, adjusted leverage of 2.97x that remains under three times EBITDA, cover of 2.96x on adjusted EBITDA, long-dated senior notes and flexible capital spending; the constraints are falling franchised earnings, free cash flow that does not cover payouts, liquidity that fell USD 116.4 million and a concentrated 2027 maturity. The trend is down on earnings and up on debt. Information needed for a firmer opinion is the covenant ratio values after 2024-12-31, the agreement definitions, management projections, a rating and peer figures.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C14
### Outlook

In the next 12 months to 24 months the headwinds are industry volume 1% to 3% below 2025, days supply of 65 days, new vehicle margin per unit that has fallen two years running, overhead at 75.60% of gross profit and the 2027 refinancing; the tailwinds are lower floor plan rates, with the weighted average down to 4.99% from 5.66%, growth in EchoPark and Powersports, and a fixed operations margin of 51.2%. Over the next three years to five years the main risks are the extension of direct and agency sales and electric vehicle adoption, which could reduce new vehicle profit pools, while the company's own plan is further acquisitions, which raise debt need before earnings arrive.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 18, 28; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 32–35, 88
### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with new vehicle demand falling toward the low end of the industry range while inventory is already high. The first operational break is days supply rising above 65 days, which forces price concessions, so gross profit per new vehicle falls below USD 2,957 and same-store unit sales fall by more than 6%. Fixed operations and finance and insurance hold up, but commission pay flexes only in part and other expenses do not, so overhead rises above 75.60% of gross profit and franchised segment income falls by more than 22.38%.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

The financial transmission is through cash and liquidity: operating cash flow on the alternative basis falls below USD 424.2 million, the USD 85.7 million gap between payouts and cash after investment widens unless payouts stop, and the floor plan deposit of USD 190.0 million and revolver availability of USD 289.5 million become the buffer. Cash plus undrawn facilities of USD 395.2 million cover the USD 561.2 million due by the end of 2027 only 0.70x, so the bridge facility, due 364 days after 2026-03-27, would have to be refinanced on lower earnings and with covenant values that creditors cannot see.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C14

Management has levers: stop repurchases, which were already absent in the third quarter, cut the dividend of USD 0.41 per share, defer the 73.71% of capital spending that is construction and real estate projects, sell or mortgage property carried at USD 2,144.3 million and reduce inventory. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress if these levers are used early, but that cannot be confirmed without covenant values, and the first observable triggers are days supply, overhead as a share of gross profit and the floor plan deposit.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C13; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-10-29_sah.htm.jsonl, pages 87, 89–91
### Overall credit view

Overall, Sonic presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring service and finance income, a franchise base spread across 24 brands and long-dated senior notes, but credit quality is constrained by falling franchised earnings, payouts funded by borrowing and a concentrated 2027 refinancing. Cash-flow durability appears adequate on the fixed operations base and weak once payouts and acquisitions are included. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on lender appetite for USD 561.2 million of bridge and mortgage debt, the level of covenant headroom and the price of the senior notes, which sit at 91.50% and 94.51% of par. The primary downside path is new vehicle margin compression on high inventory feeding through sticky overhead into lower cover, with no visible covenant headroom. Further analysis would require covenant ratio values, the agreement definitions, a rating, peer figures and management projections.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C11
Top risk: a fall in franchised segment earnings that arrives before the 2027 refinancing and while payouts continue.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C7
